# Two Approaches in EPA’s Acid Rain Program

Under Title IV, the EPA’s Acid Rain Program used different mechanisms to address sulfur dioxide (SO₂) and nitrogen oxides (NOₓ). For SO₂, an allowance represented permission to emit one ton within an aggregate cap-and-trade system.

The SO₂ program expanded in stages. Phase I began in 1995 with 263 emissions units at 110 plants. Substitution or compensating units brought the Phase I total to 445 units, and Phase II began in 2000. In 2010, the program’s final cap was 8.95 million tons—a permitted total, not a report of actual emissions.

The NOₓ component followed a separate timeline and mechanism. It began in 1996 and used a rate-based approach for certain coal-fired units, without a cap or allowance trading. The two pollutants were therefore governed by distinct rules and timelines.
